title: Police calls for service leads
summary: Counts from SDPD's published calls for service: how calls the dispatcher labelled SLEEPER, check the welfare, trespassing, 5150 or 647F ended, by the disposition code the department recorded, and the beats SLEEPER calls were sent to.

sections.heading: How calls ended
paragraphs: Every imported year file is read, each counted once per incident number: the publisher repeats an incident number when a call is updated, and the latest entry is kept. Where an incident's latest entries share a time but differ in disposition, the file does not show which came last, so the incident is counted as conflicting and under no outcome, and is left out of the calls with a disposition. Where a year's file was fetched more than once, only the latest copy is read. Only the exact call-type codes SLEEPER, CW, 602, 5150 and 647F are counted; 5150V and other variants are not.

A disposition code beginning A is an arrest, R a report and K no report required; U is unfounded. A code ending HR means the Crisis Response Team was involved, and it is counted both there and under its first letter, so those figures overlap. X, W, CAN, DUP and V are calls cancelled before a unit was sent or arrived, or duplicate calls; they are left out of the calls counted. A call with no disposition recorded is counted apart, never as no report required. Other codes are listed with their description when the disposition list is imported.

The lead is raised for the latest year with at least 100 SLEEPER calls not cancelled, marked so far when that year is not over. The other four call types are described for the same year when each has at least 100 such calls.

sections.heading: Where SLEEPER calls were sent
paragraphs: SLEEPER calls not cancelled, across every imported year, counted by the police beat of the call's address, with the neighborhood from the published beat list. The ten beats with most calls are listed, with the citywide total and the calls with no beat recorded. The lead is raised with at least 100 such calls citywide.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: A call type is the dispatcher's label when the call was entered, not a finding that anyone was unhoused. K means no report was required, not that no service was given. The file records no arrival or clear time, and the publisher leaves out sensitive call types such as domestic violence and child abuse. A beat's count is of calls to addresses in it, not a count of people. The finding lists every table it read with its source address, retrieval date and SHA-256 digest, followed by the SQL.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is not assessed: the finding restates counts and infers nothing to score.
